speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long you have had it and if you recall any specific event, like an insect bite or cut, that started it? Also, has it been spreading or changing in appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

Given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and a preceding ant bite that likely triggered a neutrophilic dermatosis, the clinical picture of a rapidly expanding, painful ulcer is most consistent with Pyoderma Gangrenosum rather than an infected bite or malignancy. I will not perform further invasive testing or imaging, as the diagnosis is primarily clinical and biopsy could induce a "pathergy" reaction that worsens the lesion.
